## Exercises

**Goal:** Scrape information from <https://www.cheese.com> to obtain a dataset of characteristics about different cheeses, and gain deeper insight into your coding process.



**Ex 1:** Locate and examine the `robots.txt` file for <https://www.cheese.com>. Summarize (in words) what you learn from the cheese.com `robots.txt` file.

It said it allow any web scrap on https://www.cheese.com, and the full URL pointing to its actual XML sitemap file is https://www.cheese.com/sitemap.xml.


**Ex 2:** Learn about the `html_attr()` function from `rvest`. Describe how this function works, and give a small code example to illustrate how it works.

It extracts data from attributes, and it returns a string.

```{r}
library(rvest)
html <- minimal_html("
  <p><a href='https://www.cheese.com/vegetarian'>vegetarian cheese</a></p>
")

html %>% 
  html_elements("p") %>%
  html_element("a") %>% 
  html_attr("href")

```


**Ex 3:** Obtain the following information for **all** cheeses in the alphabetical database <https://www.cheese.com/alphabetical/>:

- Cheese name
- URL for the cheese's webpage (e.g., <https://www.cheese.com/gouda/>)
- Whether or not the cheese has a picture (e.g., [gouda](https://www.cheese.com/gouda/) has a picture, but [bianco](https://www.cheese.com/bianco/) does not)

To be kind to the website owners, please add a 1 second pause between page queries. (Note that you can view 100 cheeses at a time.)


```{r eval=FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)

# Define the URL
url <- "https://www.cheese.com/"

# Read the HTML content from the webpage
webpage <- read_html(url)

# Extract the cheese names and URLs
page_num <- 1
more_pages <- TRUE
all_cheese_data <- list()
while(page_num<=103) {
  page_url <- paste0(url,"alphabetical/","?page=", page_num)
  webpage <- tryCatch({read_html(page_url)})

  cheese_nodes <- html_nodes(webpage, ".product-item")

    page_data <- tryCatch({
        tibble(
          cheese_name = cheese_nodes %>%
                          html_node("h3") %>% 
                          html_text(trim = TRUE),

          relative_url = cheese_nodes %>%
                            html_node("a") %>%
                            html_attr("href"), 

          has_picture = !is.na(html_node(cheese_nodes, ".image-exists"))
       ) %>%
       mutate(cheese_url = paste0(url, relative_url)) %>% 
       select(cheese_name, cheese_url, has_picture)
    })

    all_cheese_data[[page_num]] <- page_data

    page_num <- page_num + 1

    Sys.sleep(1)

}

# Create a data frame to store the results

cheese_df <- bind_rows(all_cheese_data)
write.csv(cheese_df,"cheese_df.csv")
```

**Ex 4:** When you go to a particular cheese's page (like [gouda](https://www.cheese.com/gouda/)), you'll see more detailed information about the cheese. For **just 10** of the cheeses in the database, obtain the following detailed information: milk information, country of origin, family, type, and flavour. (Just 10 to avoid overtaxing the website. Continue adding a 1 second pause between page queries.) 

```{r}
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
get_text_from_page <- function(page, css_selector) {
  nodes <- page %>% html_elements(css_selector)
  if (length(nodes) == 0) {
    return("NA")
  }else {
    page<- page %>%
        html_elements(css_selector) %>%
        html_text()
    return(page[1])
  }
}

get_cheese <- function(cheese_url) {
  Sys.sleep(1)
  cheese_page <- read_html(cheese_url)
  cheese_name <- cheese_page %>%
                 html_node("h1") %>% 
                 html_text(trim = TRUE)
  milk_information <- get_text_from_page(cheese_page, ".summary_milk")
  country_of_origin <- get_text_from_page(cheese_page, ".summary_country")
  family <- get_text_from_page(cheese_page, ".summary_family")
  type <- get_text_from_page(cheese_page, ".summary_moisture_and_type")
  flavour <- get_text_from_page(cheese_page, ".summary_taste")
  tibble(
    cheese_name = extract_text(cheese_name),
    milk_information = extract_text(milk_information),
    country_of_origin = extract_text(country_of_origin),
    family = extract_text(family),
    type = extract_text(type),
    flavour = extract_text(flavour)
  )
}

extract_text <- function(string){
  text <- string%>%
    str_extract(":[^,;\\(]+")%>%
    str_replace("^: ", "")%>%
    str_replace("\n\t\t\t\t\t\t","")
  return(text)
}

cheese_subset_df <- head(cheese_df, 10)

cheeses <- map_dfr(
  cheese_subset_df$cheese_url,
  ~ get_cheese(.x)
)
df_cheese_detail <- bind_rows(cheeses)
```
